summary: This bill requires the President to ban exports of U.S.-produced gasoline whenever the national average price reaches or exceeds $3.12 per gallon for seven consecutive days, with the ban ending only after prices stay below that threshold for seven days, though the President may grant national-interest exemptions.

scores.thoughts: The bill contains no provisions related to federal budgets, appropriations, or expenditures. It solely regulates the export of gasoline under specific price conditions. No impact on government spending.
No references to taxes, tax rates, credits, or revenue measures appear in the legislation. The focus is exclusively on export prohibitions.
The bill addresses gasoline exports and has no connection to healthcare policy, insurance, or medical services.
No provisions relate to firearms, regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
The legislation does not address immigration, visas, borders, or related enforcement.
No content pertains to reproductive rights or abortion access.
The bill makes no changes to defense budgets or military policy.

While gasoline is an energy product, the bill does not enact or modify environmental regulations, emissions standards, or conservation measures. It is an economic/trade intervention rather than an environmental one.
No provisions affect welfare programs, food assistance, or social benefits.
The bill has no relation to schools, education funding, or school choice.
No references to controlled substances, decriminalization, or drug enforcement.
The legislation does not address sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reforms.

The core mechanism of the bill is a conditional prohibition on exporting U.S.-produced gasoline, with presidential discretion for national-interest exemptions. This directly restricts exports to prioritize domestic supply, constituting a protectionist trade measure rather than promoting free trade.
No fiscal or debt-related provisions are present.
The bill contains no language concerning LGBTQ+ protections or rights.
No provisions address foreign assistance or aid programs.
The legislation is unrelated to voting rights or election procedures.
No content involves technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight.
The bill does not address labor rights, unions, or workplace regulations.
No provisions relate to religious exemptions or anti-discrimination laws.
